rationale: The refutation recorded last turn rests on draft-side operands, so this turn asks for the receipt that would make it receipt-backed: the harness now records, at every append of a configuration change, the appending node's own log (index and EntryType with the change list for ConfChangeV2 entries, capped at six entries), its pendingConfIndex and applied index before the proposal, whether its tracker was joint, and whether DisableConfChangeValidation was set. The decisive operands to confirm are the two appends at seed 35: the joint-remove change at index 2 proposed with applied=1 and pendingConfIndex=0, and the joint-add change at index 4 proposed with applied=3, pendingConfIndex=2, joint=false while the appender's own log already contained the joint change at index 2. If the receipt reproduces that pair, the rejected history is attributable to the harness's restart modelling - a node restored with a non-joint tracker over an applied joint change - and the refutation stands on execution rather than on a draft-side run; if it does not, the operands will show which state actually produced the append and the question reopens. No stop: the run has time for the receipt and the follow-up interpretation.

scope.description: Sixteenth revision of the same fixed harness. Probes A-C and the deterministic cases (joint-change order, stale guard, no-op joint removal) are unchanged. The sweep adds append-side instrumentation: for every configuration change it proposes, it records the appending node's own log summary (index and EntryType, with transition and change list for EntryConfChangeV2, capped at six entries), pendingConfIndex, applied index and tracker jointness immediately before the proposal, and the DisableConfChangeValidation flag, emitting a conf_change_appended event when an EntryConfChangeV2 is appended. The rejection operands (decoded log_types, applied_before, applying_before, reapplied_entry, joint_now, entry index/term/change count) and the summary counters are unchanged.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft, SetHardState, raftLog.slice, proto.Unmarshal); no production logic is modified.
The own-log summary is read from the appending node immediately after the proposal is delivered, so it reflects that node's log including the appended entry.
The append events are emitted for every configuration change proposed in the run, so the decisive pair can be located by seed and step.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps, as before, pick one of MsgHup, MsgProp, tick(), isolate, recover, TransferLeader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change, target from node 4 or a non-leader member, half JointImplicit), a restart of a random node, or persist/apply of all nodes; when a configuration change is proposed, record the appending node's pendingConfIndex, applied index and jointness before the proposal and its own log summary after, emitting conf_change_appended for EntryConfChangeV2 appends; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 with lag and recovered conf-change applies, evaluate the invariants and the liveness witness, and finally emit invariant_sweep_summary.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation as the previous sweep execution, with append-side instrumentation added so the proposer's own state and log are observable at the moment a configuration change is appended. A draft-side run reported for seed 35 that the index-4 joint-add change was appended with applied=3, pendingConfIndex=2, joint_before=false while the appender's own log already held the joint change at index 2, which is construction feedback only and is why isolated execution is requested.
